descriptor: Generic formulations exporter building injectables and medical devices
lede: A Surat pharma company that exports generic tablets and capsules under its own registrations to Africa, Latin America and Asia, and is adding injectables, medical devices and consumer brands through part-owned subsidiaries. Revenue has grown about 56% a year for four years and management aims to triple it again in three, but cash flow lags profit, receivables have ballooned and the company holds no earnings calls.

short_version.text: Consolidated revenue ₹129 Cr in FY26 (+48%) with EBITDA margin up to 21.8% and PAT ₹19 Cr; Q1 FY27 revenue +43% and EBITDA +65%. Plants run at only ~40% utilisation, 2,534 product registrations are pending, and an injectables plant starts in October 2026.

₹45 Cr of profit over FY22-26 against –₹16 Cr of operating cash flow; debtor days reached ~209 and borrowings ₹73 Cr. Most subsidiaries are 51-60% owned, ₹27 Cr was lent to related parties in FY26, and shareholders are asked to let the chairman's pay rise to ₹25 lakh a month.
~24x trailing earnings and ~19x EV/EBITDA, against Marksans at 27x, Lincoln at 11x and Kwality Pharma at 45x.

blocks.text: Trident Lifeline registers generic formulations (anti-infectives, anti-malarials, anti-diabetics, vitamins and more) in emerging markets and supplies them under its own brands through distributors, using its Surat liquids and ointments plant, a 51%-owned oral-solids subsidiary (TNS Pharma) and contract manufacturers. Newer subsidiaries make IV cannulas and infusion sets (Trident Mediquip, 60%), injectables (TLL Parenterals, 51%, from October 2026), herbal products (TLL Wellness, 51%) and 'YES' cosmetics (TLL Elements, 100%).

items.text: Each export registration costs ~$5,000 and takes 1.5-3 years; once approved it earns for years and keeps rivals out.
Plants are built only after demand is validated, keeping capital needs low.
Domestic tenders use spare capacity at thinner margins.
Listed on BSE SME in 2022; revenue from ₹22 Cr (FY22) to ₹129 Cr (FY26).
Bought or set up TNS Pharma, Trident Mediquip, TLL Parenterals, TLL Wellness and TLL Elements in 2022-25.
Acquired 50,000 sq m of land for a five-to-six-unit pharma complex, starting with a cephalosporin plant.

items.text: Promoters hold 62.5% (Desai family ~38% incl. a family trust, Gajera family ~17%, Jariwala ~5%); no pledge.
Foreign institutions cut holdings from 7.7% to 1.2% in a year; shareholders still only ~1,050.
₹27 Cr lent to related parties in FY26, all repayable on demand: ₹15 Cr to subsidiaries and ₹12 Cr to other related parties (₹7 Cr outstanding).
AGM resolution lets the chairman be paid up to ₹25 lakh a month, above the profit-linked cap; actual FY26 pay was ~8x the median employee.
Auditors made revenue recognition (rebates and discounts) a key audit matter.

items.name: Bull
items.text: On track to triple: ~₹270 Cr revenue in FY28 at a 15% PAT margin (₹40 Cr), valued at 25x.

items.name: Base
items.text: ~28% growth a year to ~₹210 Cr at a 13% margin (₹27 Cr), valued at 20x.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Collections and new plants stall: ~₹160 Cr at a 10% margin (₹16 Cr), valued at 14x.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Trident has grown fast from a small base on a registration-led model and has capacity to grow further without much capex. The valuation is not stretched for the growth, but cash conversion, receivables, related-party lending and thin disclosure are real concerns; the injectables start-up and a fall in receivable days are the things to watch.
